videos.script: You have typed go build and go test hundreds of times by now. This lesson is about what they actually do, because that decides how long you wait and what you can trust. {{run}} First, go run. It looks like an interpreter, and it is a compiler. It builds an executable, keeps it in a cache, and starts it. Watch the exit code, though. go run does not pass it on. {{cache}} Then the build cache. The first build of hits takes seconds. The second takes a few hundredths of one. Every compiled package is kept, keyed by its content, not by a date. {{install}} Next, go install. It puts your program on the PATH, and it fetches other people's tools at an exact version, without touching your go.mod. {{test}} Then go test, the way you run it all day. One test or a group of subtests, the fast ones only, stop at the first failure, output a program can read. And what the word cached in its output really means. {{doc}} Last, go doc and go list. They answer questions from the source on your disk. One of those answers finds a bug in hits that no test had caught.
